final_message:
The oracle provider now emits `FixedIn` entries with an `Arch` key only when the fix differs by architecture. The unit tests pass (913). The 15 `tests/quality/test_configure.py` failures are an unrelated `yardstick` import error that I didn't touch.

- **Arch-aware parsing:** The parser reads the `Oracle Linux arch is <arch>` criteria in each ELSA and tracks the architecture for every package version. Changes are in `oval_parser.py` and `parser.py`.
- **When `Arch` appears:** If every version of a package ships on all of that package's architectures, you get one arch-less entry per version. That covers a single shared fix and several rebuilds that each ship everywhere. Otherwise each entry carries its own `Arch`, e.g. `8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3` for aarch64 and `8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3` for x86_64.
- **Package on one arch only:** A package built for a single architecture, with one version, stays arch-less. That is my reading of "differentiates the fix", so say if you want those tagged.
- **Schema:** I added `schema/vulnerability/os/schema-1.1.1.json`, which is 1.1.0 plus an optional `FixedIn.Arch` string. A new `ORACLE_OS_SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.1.1"` in `schema.py` is used only by the oracle provider; all others still get 1.1.0.
- **Ordering:** Output order is now deterministic, with `Arch` added to the sort keys.
- **Tests:** I updated the oracle snapshots to the 1.1.1 schema URL and added `test_parse_arch`. It covers the differing-fix, shared-fix and multiple-rebuild cases.

I also wrote `answer.json` in the repository root as requested.

The mock fixtures contain no arch criteria, so the new test uses a synthetic OVAL. The `Oracle Linux arch is <arch>` comment format and the nesting of arch criteria inside the criteria tree come from my recollection of Oracle's OVAL, not from the real feed. I haven't checked them against it.

    """

def _collapse_arches(pkgs: set[tuple[str, str, str | None]]) -> set[tuple[str, str, str | None]]:
    """
    Reduce (package, version, arch) tuples so that Arch is only retained where the architecture differentiates
    the fix: a package whose every version ships on all of the package's architectures (e.g. a single shared fix,
    or several rebuilds that each cover all arches) yields one arch-less entry per version.
    """
    arches_by_pkg: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
    arches_by_pkg_version: dict[tuple[str, str], set[str]] = {}
    for name, version, arch in pkgs:
        if arch:
            arches_by_pkg.setdefault(name, set()).add(arch)
            arches_by_pkg_version.setdefault((name, version), set()).add(arch)

    collapsed = set()
    for name, version, arch in pkgs:
        all_arches = arches_by_pkg.get(name, set())
        if arch and arches_by_pkg_version[(name, version)] != all_arches:
            collapsed.add((name, version, arch))
        elif arch and any(arches_by_pkg_version[(name, v)] != all_arches for (n, v) in arches_by_pkg_version if n == name):
            # another version of this package is arch-specific, so keep arch on every entry
            collapsed.add((name, version, arch))
        else:
            collapsed.add((name, version, None))
    return collapsed

def _arch_oval(criteria: str) -> str:
    return f"""<oval_definitions xmlns="http://oval.mitre.org/XMLSchema/oval-definitions-5"><definitions>
<definition id="oval:com.oracle.elsa:def:20224803" version="1" class="patch"><metadata>
<title>ELSA-2022-4803:  Moderate: rsyslog security update  (MODERATE)</title>
<affected family="unix"><platform>Oracle Linux 7</platform></affected>
<reference source="elsa" ref_id="ELSA-2022-4803" ref_url="http://linux.oracle.com/errata/ELSA-2022-4803.html"/>
<description>d</description>
<advisory><severity>MODERATE</severity><issued date="2022-06-01"/></advisory></metadata>
<criteria operator="AND"><criterion comment="Oracle Linux 7 is installed"/>{criteria}</criteria>
</definition></definitions></oval_definitions>"""


def _arch_block(arch, versions):
    pkgs = "".join(f'<criterion comment="rsyslog is earlier than {v}"/>' for v in versions)
    return f'<criteria operator="AND"><criterion comment="Oracle Linux arch is {arch}"/><criteria operator="OR">{pkgs}</criteria></criteria>'


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "per_arch, expected",
    [
        # fix differs per arch -> Arch retained
        (
            {"aarch64": ["8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3"], "x86_64": ["8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3"]},
            [("8.24.0-57.0.1.el7_9.3", "x86_64"), ("8.24.0-57.0.4.el7_9.3", "aarch64")],
        ),
        # shared fix -> no Arch, single entry
        (
            {"aarch64": ["8.24.0-57.el7"], "x86_64": ["8.24.0-57.el7"]},
            [("8.24.0-57.el7", None)],
        ),
        # several rebuilds, each for all arches -> arch-less, one per version
        (
            {"aarch64": ["8.24.0-1.el7", "8.24.0-2.el7"], "x86_64": ["8.24.0-1.el7", "8.24.0-2.el7"]},
            [("8.24.0-1.el7", None), ("8.24.0-2.el7", None)],
        ),
    ],
)
def test_parse_arch(tmpdir, per_arch, expected):
    path = tmpdir / "oval.xml"
    path.write_text(_arch_oval("<criteria operator='OR'>" + "".join(_arch_block(a, v) for a, v in per_arch.items()) + "</criteria>"), encoding="utf-8")
    subject = parser.Parser(workspace=workspace.Workspace(tmpdir, "test", create=True))
    vuln_dict = subject._parse_oval_data(str(path), subject.config)
    _, record = vuln_dict[("ELSA-2022-4803", "ol:7")]
    fixed = record["Vulnerability"]["FixedIn"]
    assert [(f["Version"], f.get("Arch")) for f in fixed] == expected
    assert all(("Arch" in f) == (f.get("Arch") is not None) for f in fixed)
EOF
